focus: Dialog_DungeonFinder (window flags, per-frame highlight drawing, static state), the four Dialog_WorldSearch/WorldSearchElement patches, the enteredBy save format, and the UV fix in WorldDrawLayer_Dungeons
diffSource: since build 3 (2026-10-06T22:23:51Z), the last reviewed build, from the build log

findings.title: Finder origin on the orbit layer logs an out-of-range tile error per dungeon on every recalculation
findings.detail: Dialog_DungeonFinder.Recalculate computes Find.WorldGrid.ApproxDistanceInTiles(origin, tile). WorldGrid forwards to tileA.Layer (the origin's layer), and PlanetLayer.ApproxDistanceInTiles(int,int) calls GetTileCenter on the surface tile id within that layer. Odyssey's orbit layer is built with 5 subdivisions (Defs/Odyssey/WorldLayerSettingsDefs/PlanetLayerSettings.xml:9) against 10 for the surface, so most surface tile ids exceed its TilesCount, and PlanetLayer.GetTileCenter(int) (PlanetLayer.cs:689-698) logs an error for each one. It triggers when the origin is an orbital player home (a gravship in orbit). That can be the constructor default (Find.AnyPlayerHomeMap) or a pick from OriginOptions, which lists every IsPlayerHome map. It repeats on every slider step. Fix in Recalculate: only measure when origin.Layer is the surface. Otherwise project the origin first, e.g. compare origin.Layer.GetTileCenter(origin).normalized with surface.GetTileCenter(id).normalized and pass GenMath.SphericalDistance of the two to surface.ApproxDistanceInTiles(float).

findings.title: MarkEntered is never called, so the 'hide dungeons a ticked pawn entered' filter never hides anything
findings.detail: Searching Source/ for MarkEntered finds only its definition in DungeonWorldComponent.cs. enteredBy is therefore always empty, and both the HasEntered check in Recalculate and the new save field are inert. Call MarkEntered(tileId, pawn) wherever a caravan enters a dungeon (where the per-use world object is made), or hold back the party-filter wording until that exists.

findings.title: Regenerating dungeons keeps enteredBy keyed by the old tile ids
findings.detail: Generate() replaces tiles and levels but leaves enteredBy alone. After the dev 'Regenerate dungeons' action, or a genVersion bump, entries can mark a different new dungeon as entered or linger unused. Clearing enteredBy at the top of Generate() avoids it. This only matters once MarkEntered is called.

findings.title: Static ticked HashSet<Pawn> keeps the previous game's pawns alive until the finder is reopened
findings.detail: ticked is static and holds Pawn references. It is only pruned by RemoveWhere in the constructor, so after a load or a return to the main menu the old game's pawns, and everything they reference, stay reachable. Clearing it when the window closes, or storing load ids, would avoid this. The memory cost is real but small.

findings.title: Changed setting defaults silently move players who never touched them
findings.detail: Scribe_Values.Look(ref spacing, "spacing", DefaultSpacing) does not write a value equal to its default. Players who left spacing at 3, roughness at 3 or opacity at 0.6 have nothing saved and now get 10, 7 and 0.4. Spacing and roughness only affect new worlds; opacity changes at once. This is probably intended; worth a changelog line.

findings.title: OdysseyPatch's InitializeSearchSet postfix may snapshot the search set before dungeons are added
findings.detail: odysseypatch.1trickpwnyta also postfixes Dialog_WorldSearch.InitializeSearchSet. In non-full-search mode it calls Notify_CommonSearchChanged synchronously, which copies SearchSet into allElements. If it runs before this postfix, dungeon elements reach the results only on the next filter change. In practice that is the first keystroke, so nothing breaks.

findings.title: Count strings don't handle the singular: "1 dungeons match", "1 tiles"
findings.detail: TUBAD_Finder_Matches and TUBAD_Finder_Tiles always use the plural. Dialog_DungeonFinder.cs:203 and :223 pass the raw count, so a single result reads "1 dungeons match" and a distance of 1 reads "1 tiles". This is cosmetic. Adding _Singular keys, or wording that doesn't need a plural ("Matches: {0}"), would fix it.
